page: Amazon Web Services t4g.medium is a burstable general-purpose instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and custom AWS Graviton2 processors. The underlying hardware features an arm64 architecture utilizing ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 cores clocked at 2.5 GHz. The instance is provisioned with 2 burstable vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with 1 thread per core, alongside 4.0 GB of memory (2.0 GB per core). Cache resources include 64 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and a 32 MB L3 cache pool. Hardware-accelerated AES cryptography instructions are available, while x86-specific vector extensions and simultaneous multithreading are absent.

Hardware bundling is minimal; the instance includes no local storage and no dedicated hardware accelerators, featuring 0 GPUs. Network performance has a baseline of 0 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned, requiring reliance on elastic network attachments and EBS storage for persistent operations.

Benchmark results demonstrate modest computational throughput constrained by core count and burstable resource allocation. In single-core stress-ng testing, the instance achieved an average result of 1512.88, while multi-core stress-ng scored 2867.47, categorizing it in the lower quartile. Geekbench scores registered 927.0 for single-core and 1677.0 for multi-core. PassMark CPU testing showed a total score of 1274.3 with database operations scoring 1232.27. Memory throughput reached 35.15 GB/sec for uncached read-only blocks and 17.23 GB/sec for uncached write operations.

Targeted operational metrics place the instance in low throughput brackets across continuous services. Static web serving throughput measured 2.23 GB/sec, while Redis SET performance hit 2.11 million operations per second. Light language model inference utilizing a small 135M model managed 72.69 tokens/sec for prompt processing and 19.98 tokens/sec for generation, while larger models (7B and 70B) are unsupported by the available memory footprint. As an entry-level burstable instance, it offers a budget-oriented hardware footprint best applied to low-traffic microservices, light developer environments, small database caches, and periodic background automation.

The instance does not include integrated local storage or GPU hardware, and operates with a 0 Gbps baseline network capability. Performance benchmarks place the instance largely in entry-level percentiles, recording a Geekbench multi-core score of 1677.0, PassMark CPU score of 1274.3, and Redis SET throughput of 2.11 million operations per second.
